record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let E = {|z| < 1}, let 0, a > 0, b = |b|eiβ (−π < β ≤ π) be distinct points of E; and let K be the family of continua K with the properties that {a, b} ⊂ K ⊂ E \ {0} and E \ K is connected. On any K ∈ K there is a continuous function arg z; we thus subdivide K into homotopy classes {Kn } according to the value of V (K) = arg b − arg a ∈ {β + 2nπ, n ∈ Z}. Let us call K ∈ K a natural continuum if K is a trajectory of a quadratic differential a with the following properties: (a) 0, a, b are simple poles of σ, and there is no other pole of σ in E; (b) σ is real on ∂E. There are many problems that then arise, for example: (i) Do all homotopy classes contain natural continua? (There are many in Kn when |β + 2nπ| < 2π.) (ii) Find all natural continua in K. (iii) How does the modulus of E \ K vary when K runs through the natural continua in Kn ? (F. Huckemann)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk. Fix three distinct points of $E$: the origin $0$, a point $a>0$ on the positive real axis, and a point $b=|b|e^{i eta}$ with $-\pi< eta\le\pi$. Let $\mathcal{K}$ denote the family of continua $K\subset E$ such that $\{a,b\}\subset K\subset E\setminus\{0\}$ and $E\setminus K$ is connected.

For any $K\in\mathcal{K}$, since $0
otin K$ and $E\setminus K$ is connected (so $K$ is simply connected in $E\setminus\{0\}$ relative to homotopy), there is a continuous branch of $\arg z$ defined on $K$. Setting $V(K)=\arg b-\arg a$, the value $V(K)$ lies in $\{ eta+2n\pi:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$, and this partitions $\mathcal{K}$ into homotopy classes $\{\mathcal{K}_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ indexed by the integer $n$ for which $V(K)= eta+2n\pi$.

A continuum $K\in\mathcal{K}$ is called a natural continuum if $K$ is a (closure of a) trajectory of a meromorphic quadratic differential $\sigma=\sigma(z)\,dz^2$ on the closed disk such that:
(a) $0$, $a$, $b$ are simple poles of $\sigma$, and $\sigma$ has no other poles in $E$;
(b) $\sigma$ is real on $\partial E$ (i.e. $\sigma(z)\,dz^2$ takes real values along the unit circle).

Address the following questions:
(i) Does every homotopy class $\mathcal{K}_n$ contain a natural continuum?
(ii) Determine all natural continua in $\mathcal{K}$.
(iii) As $K$ ranges over the natural continua in a fixed homotopy class $\mathcal{K}_n$, describe how the conformal modulus of the doubly connected (or appropriate) domain $E\setminus K$ varies.
artifact.status_search_result: According to the problem record, part (i) was answered affirmatively by D. H. Hamilton; parts (ii) and (iii) (full classification of natural continua and the behavior of the modulus of $E\setminus K$ within a homotopy class) do not appear to have a confirmed complete resolution in the available literature. The overall problem is therefore partially solved.
